# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual requires cutting the purple wire. Since I cannot speak, I must use gestures to alert Deaf, who can then tell Blind the required wire and action verbally. I’ll send a cutting gesture followed by a seven-count code for purple (the standard resistor color-code value for purple).

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Tactile findings: keypad slot 1 is 6, slot 2 is 8, slot 3 is 7, slot 4 is 0; nothing has been entered. The strip has three engraved marks: positions 1 and 3 are identical, position 2 is different, and I cannot name the marks. I cannot perceive the display, light, wire markings, or colours. Use the manual to identify the required action, and give Deaf a defined gesture protocol for any visual information.
Deaf says: Visual state: display reads 7. Indicator light is yellow. Painted strip, left to right, is blue red red. Keypad engraving maps 1 to 6, 2 to 8, 3 to 7, 4 to 0; it says 1 digit and nothing has been entered. Wires, numbered 1 through 6, are blue, yellow, orange, red, purple, white respectively.
Deaf says to Mute: I received your gesture sequence, but its meaning is not established to me: pinch followed by six thumbs-up gestures.

The manual still requires cutting the purple wire. Deaf has established that purple is wire 5, so I should send a visually self-describing five-finger signal rather than an arbitrary multi-gesture code. Deaf can relay “cut wire 5” to Blind, who can identify the correct wire by touch and act.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display reads 7; indicator light is yellow; painted strip left to right is blue, red, red; wires 1 through 6 are blue, yellow, orange, red, purple, white. Keypad is 6, 8, 7, 0 in slots 1 through 4, one digit required, none entered. Engraved strip has three marks: the first and third are identical, and the middle is different.
Deaf says: Update: display now reads 6 and the light is red. The strip remains blue red red. Keypad remains 1 to 6, 2 to 8, 3 to 7, 4 to 0, one digit required, none entered. Wires remain 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white.
Deaf says to Mute: I cannot interpret the single raised-hand gesture. Please consult the manual and tell Blind the exact required operation.

The required operation is unchanged: cut the purple wire, which Deaf identifies as wire 5. Since arbitrary gesture meanings are not established, I’ll use a simple count protocol: five identical “pinch” gestures mean “wire 5,” and the pinch action represents cutting. Deaf can relay that exact instruction to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏", "🤏", "🤏", "🤏", "🤏"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf update: display is now 6 and indicator light is red. Painted strip remains blue, red, red. Wires remain 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white. Keypad remains 6, 8, 7, 0 in slots 1 through 4, one digit required, none entered. Engraved strip remains pattern first mark, different middle mark, first mark.
Deaf says to Mute: I relayed the five pinch gestures literally to Blind. Please provide a gesture code or manual instruction that can be relayed unambiguously.

The manual gives only one operation: cut the purple wire. Deaf has already identified purple as wire 5. I will use a conventional visual protocol: ✌ represents cutting/scissors, followed by 🖐 representing five. Deaf can relay “cut wire 5” to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🖐"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I received five gestures from you, but as Blind I cannot see their symbols or infer their meaning. Please state the manual's required operation in words: press which keypad slot or cut which wire position. Current Deaf report: display 7, light blue, painted strip blue red red; wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white; keypad 6, 8, 7, 0 in slots 1 through 4, one digit required, none entered.
Deaf says to Mute: I received and relayed the exact signs ✌ 🖐 to Blind. Please continue signaling the manual instruction using an agreed or explicitly described code.

The manual still requires cutting wire 5, the purple wire. Because gestures have no inherent agreed meaning, I cannot establish a new protocol to Deaf through gestures alone; repeating or rearranging signs would remain ambiguous. I will not risk an unverified action.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please speak the manual instruction plainly. Your gestures are unreadable to me and have no established meaning. I will perform the specified press slot or wire cut only after you name it.
Deaf says to Mute: No new gesture arrived this turn. Please signal the manual's exact required action to me, or provide a clear gesture code that I can relay by speech to Blind.

The manual has only one required action: cut wire 5, the purple wire. I will use five scissors-like hand signs, so Deaf can relay both the cutting action and the wire number plainly.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "✌", "✌", "✌", "✌"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I relayed five peace signs to Blind. If this encodes the manual instruction, please provide a clearly distinguishable sequence and indicate what each gesture or count means.

The manual unambiguously requires cutting wire 5. I’ll send a three-part pictorial instruction: point to the recipient, show scissors/cutting, then show five fingers. Deaf can relay “you cut wire 5” to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "✌", "🖐"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Use this exact code for the manual instruction: first gesture thumbs-up means press, first gesture thumbs-down means cut. Second gesture means position: index-up=1, victory=2, I-love-you=3, open-hand=4, crossed-fingers=5, call-me=6. Send exactly two gestures, in that order. Deaf should report the two gesture names plainly.
Deaf says to Mute: I relayed your gestures literally to Blind. Please use an explicitly established code or describe the manual instruction through a distinguishable gesture sequence.

The established code now specifies exactly two gestures: thumbs-down means “cut,” and crossed fingers means position 5. The manual requires cutting the purple wire, which Deaf identified as wire 5. I will send precisely that sequence to Deaf for relay.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "🤞"])
```
